content.comment_body: I'm studying electronics and doing my final internship. The company has two [product_name] modules (12/24VRC), which are fully wired and will be used to control the building's lighting. My issue is: how do I switch off all the building's lights when one part is linked to the first module and the other to the second?

Hello, from what you've described, you have two [product_name] modules controlling lighting and want a general 'All Lights OFF' feature. There are many complex ways to achieve this, like exchanging data between the modules if it's possible. You can use EIB/KNX bus to communicate between several [product_name] modules, but you will need an EIB/KNX expansion module for each one. The easiest method is to connect the sensor (that switches off all lights) to the input of both modules and program them to turn off their outputs accordingly. Hope this helps.

Hi [user_name], This can be solved on the device in different ways: 1) For up to 10 meters: use [product_name] panel plus a module with expansion modules. [url] 2) Use two modules with expansion modules. [url] or see this discussion: [url] 3) Use a communication module for EIB/KNX or AS-i. [url] 4) Ethernet (coming soon).
Thanks for your help. I understand I need to buy an EIB bus system to connect two [product_name] modules, but I'm unsure about which model to choose and how to do the connection.

Here's an example of communication between two modules using EIB/KNX: [url]. [user_name] can provide more details about this issue. The [product_name] module is versatile and could make solving the problem easier. I recommend using [product_name] in EIB networks, especially if one already exists.

Currently, everything is wired in the [product_name] modules: inputs are buttons and outputs are lamps. One module has 20 inputs, the other has 16. I've programmed the first module to control its outputs. I want the button connected to the first module to be able to switch all the building's lights, including those managed by the second module. In the diagram you sent, I have modules 1 and 2, but need to purchase module 3 and possibly module 4 to connect the two [product_name] modules. [url] Thanks.

Hi [user_name], If you integrate more devices, you'll need to handle two software tools ([product_name] programming tool and ETS) and understand the bus structure. This is a solid approach for building automation and has been used for more than 20 years.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants are working on synchronized lighting control using two [product_name] modules. They face obstacles with inter-device communication for an 'All Lights Off' function due to wiring and networking constraints. Solutions discussed range from straightforward wiring changes to implementing advanced bus systems, but users are unsure about which communication modules to select and how to connect them. Adding bus configuration software increases complexity for those inexperienced with such automation technology.
analysis.user_expectations: The main expectation is for a simple method to control all building lights from a single point, despite being wired to two different modules. Users want clear instructions regarding which communication hardware to purchase and guidance on connecting and configuring multiple modules together.
